why: The code puts 'else return -1' inside the loop, so the method gives an answer after checking only arr[0]. It is written as if 'else' meant 'if no element matches'. It also returns the first match rather than the last, so the new code is wrong and cannot reach L4.

concepts.quote: if (arr[i] == key) return i; else return -1;
concepts.why: It reads 'else' as 'otherwise, after all are checked', but in Java the else runs on the first mismatch and its return ends the search at once.

concepts.quote: for (...) { if (arr[i] == key) return i; else return -1; }
concepts.why: Both branches return, so the loop body runs at most once and the loop never goes past index 0, unlike the multi-pass search the task needs.
It correctly uses arr[i] to mean the element at position i, and returns i as the position, but this is not applied any further.
It writes a valid comparison expression, but does not evaluate it for any values.
It uses a correct conditional with a boolean test, but the reasoning about it stops there.
The answer says nothing about declaring an array.
